title: AMD CEO Visits Samsung for HBM, Samsung Wants Foundry Orders in Return
key_facts: Lisa Su met Samsung's Jun Young-hyun at Samsung's Seocho office in Seoul on 7 Oct, for a little over three hours including dinner.
Su said she had 'a very good discussion' and that Samsung is 'an excellent partner'.
Asked about foundry progress, she said 'Overall, we have a very broad partnership', giving no specifics.
Samsung and AMD signed an MOU in March on HBM4 and server DDR5 supply and agreed to discuss producing AMD products at Samsung's foundry.
Industry reading: AMD needs more HBM while Samsung seeks more foundry orders.
Business Korea: Su also met SK hynix president Kwak Noh-jung the same day.
quote_evidence: Su arrived at Samsung Electronics' Seocho office building in Seocho-gu, Seoul, at about 4:44 p.m., met with Vice Chair Jun, and left the building at about 7:58 p.m.
Asked if there had been progress in foundry cooperation, she said, "Overall, we have a very broad partnership."

In the industry, there is an interpretation that the meeting was intended to bridge differences between AMD, which needs to expand its HBM supply, and Samsung Electronics, which is seeking to increase foundry orders.
why_it_matters_hint: Memory supply and possible foundry link between AMD and Samsung; no deal announced.
notes: TechPowerUp page (consent wall) unreadable; story read at Chosun Biz (own reporting) and corroborated by Business Korea (also reports Su met SK hynix's Kwak Noh-jung the same day). The 'memory for foundry orders' framing in TechPowerUp's headline is an industry interpretation, so stated as such.
